key_insight: SPOD-GPR combines spectral reduced-order modelling with Gaussian processes to improve prediction accuracy and uncertainty calibration beyond training parameters and time horizons.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports uncertainty-aware flow surrogates for many-query analysis and potential real-time digital-twin applications.
method: Compress states with parametric POD, then apply windowed frequency transforms and SPOD at retained energetic frequencies.
Learn parameter-dependent bases with GPR on local Grassmann charts after Procrustes alignment.
Predict spectral coefficients using parameter-based and parameter-conditioned autoregressive models, with joint pathwise posterior sampling.
evidence_signal: Across four parametric examples—two Kuramoto–Sivashinsky regimes, cylinder flow and elliptic-obstacle flow—SPOD-GPR reduced normalised mean absolute error versus POD-GPR and improved uncertainty calibration, especially for the fluid flows.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify runtime or accuracy gains, so real-time suitability and robustness to larger extrapolations remain to be established.
paper_title: Parametric spatio-temporal reduced-order modelling via Spectral Proper Orthogonal Decomposition and Gaussian Process Regression
